title: How Doctors Unblock Your Heart Without Opening Your Chest
sources: Coronary artery disease: fatty plaque builds up inside the coronary arteries and narrows them, reducing blood flow to the heart muscle (NHLBI, 'Coronary Heart Disease')

Coronary angioplasty / PCI: a catheter is inserted into an artery in the wrist (radial) or groin and guided to the narrowed coronary artery; a balloon on the catheter is inflated to widen the artery, pressing the plaque against the wall, and a stent (small wire-mesh tube) is usually left in place to keep it open (NHS, 'Coronary angioplasty and stent insertion'; NHLBI, 'Percutaneous Coronary Intervention')
The procedure is done under local anaesthetic, usually with a sedative, so the patient is awake; many people go home the same day or the next day (NHS, 'Coronary angioplasty – What happens')
